title: Cost & Reliability Tactical Huddle - Velocity
summary: Quarterly tactical check-in focused on an unexpected usage spike, cost impact from increased token volume, and a short-term reliability mitigation plan. Agreed to run a targeted cache/batching experiment and provide security docs for upcoming audit request.
topics: usage spike analysis and root cause
short-term optimization experiments (caching, batching, model variant)
roadmap alignment and upcoming audit/security ask
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-07 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Chris (Head of ML - Velocity), Maya (Platform Eng), Samir (CTO - joined 00:25)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick agenda — usage spike, cost impact, a couple reliability blips last week, and then quick plan for experiments. is that aligned?
[00:12] Chris: yeah, sounds good. i'll start with the spike context — we saw a 3x increase in inference calls on tuesday, mostly from a new QA flow we rolled out. it wasn't traffic from production users, it was our internal synthetic runner.
[00:28] Maya: to add — that runner was using full conversation history every time, so context lengths ballooned. we didn't realize it until the bill showed up, honestly.
[00:40] Priya: ok that maps to token cost increasing. do you have a distribution of sequence lengths? even approximate?
[00:47] Chris: yeah, i'll paste the graph after. median went from 512 to about 2,400 tokens for a bunch of calls. some outliers hit 10k.
[00:57] Jordan: ouch. for us that explains the proportional jump in tokens and cost. also explains the KV cache pressure — our runtime saw heavier KV cache churn which increased latency.
[01:10] Maya: one of the incidents we saw was a service timeout when the autoscaler tried to spin up additional workers. we had a couple 502s for about 10 minutes. not large user impact but alarming.
[01:22] Priya: thanks. quick Q — are you on hosted or dedicated?
[01:25] Chris: hosted API. we moved off earlier this year to simplify.
[01:29] Priya: ok. that matters for what autoscaling knobs are available and for cache locality. on hosted we can recommend batching and prefix caching tweaks.
[01:38] Jordan: also want to flag quotas — sounds like the synthetic runner didn't respect rate limits. maybe we need a guardrail.
[01:45] Maya: yeah, we missed the new token quotas in the integration.
[01:48] Samir (joined): sorry i'm late — jumped from another meeting. heard spike and timeouts, is this still active?
[01:54] Chris: mostly contained; we cut the runner and throttled the QA environment. but we want a plan so it doesn't happen again.
[02:03] Priya: recommendation 1 — short experiment: enable prefix/KV caching for the common conversation start, and a continuous batching window increase from 10ms to 25ms for that QA flow. that should reduce per-token compute and amortize cost.
[02:19] Maya: would that affect latency for real users? our SLO is 200 ms P95.
[02:24] Priya: for production paths we can keep 10ms; only target the QA runner route. Redwood supports route-level batching and cache policies.
[02:33] Jordan: recommendation 2 — model variant routing. for QA use a 7B quantized variant, keep 13B or higher for production. that reduces cost a lot.
[02:42] Chris: how different is output quality? our regression tests are sensitive.
[02:46] Priya: you'll see some delta on edge cases, but for QA correctness checks it's acceptable. we'll run an eval on your prompt set.
[02:53] Maya: also, can we get a preview of cost delta?
[02:56] Jordan: yes — we'll run a quick cost projection and share by EOD.
[03:01] Chris: ok. security ask — audit team wants SOC2 artifacts and a KMS diagram for how keys are used. they want it by next friday.
[03:09] Jordan: we have that; i'll share the security package and the KMS integration doc.
[03:13] Priya: one more reliability note — when autoscale happened we saw cold start overhead for some model variants. i'll capture the exact latency traces and share.
[03:22] Maya: do you have recommendations for warm pools or reserved capacity? we're cost-conscious but might invest if it prevents customer-facing outages.
[03:30] Jordan: short-term: reserved warm pools for critical routes (small footprint) or small dedicated burst reservation. mid-term: consider Dedicated for throughput predictability. but that's a contract decision.
[03:41] Samir: what about fallbacks — if higher model is unavailable can we automatically route to a cheaper model and tag the response? we want transparency in logs.
[03:49] Priya: yes, Redwood supports automated fallback policy and it can annotate responses with model variant metadata. we can also surface it in the Console logs and traces.
[04:00] Chris: that's important. okay, so experiments: 1) enable prefix cache for QA route; 2) bump batching window for QA route; 3) route QA to 7B quantized variant; 4) generate cost projection; 5) share security docs. timeline?
[04:15] Jordan: propose experiment window 72 hours after we flip settings; cost projection EOD; security docs today; latency traces from Priya tomorrow.
[04:24] Maya: can Redwood make the route-level changes or do we need to?
[04:28] Priya: we can make them in hosted for you, but want you to confirm the route name and exact header the runner uses. we'll need an integration flag to scope it.
[04:38] Chris: i'll put the route id in the shared notes.
[04:41] Samir: question on logging retention — for audit we need 90 days of request-level metadata. what's feasible?
[04:47] Jordan: hosted default is 30 days; we have an add-on for 90+ day retention. i'll include pricing in the follow-up.
[04:55] Chris: ok. any blockers from Redwood side?
[04:58] Priya: nothing immediate — just need the route id and the prompt eval set for regression checks.
[05:05] Jordan: recap of next steps, and we'll book a 30-minute check-in after the 72-hour experiment window to review outcomes and decide next steps.
[05:12] Maya: thanks, that's helpful.
[05:14] Samir: thanks all.

Auto-generated notes (optional):
- Observed 3x spike driven by internal QA runner; median context went to ~2400 tokens; outliers 10k.
- Cost drivers: longer context and high frequency; KV cache churn increased latency and minor 502s during autoscale.
- Proposed mitigations: route-scoped prefix caching, increase batching window for QA route, route QA to 7B quantized model variant, targeted warm pool or burst reservation consideration.

End of transcript.

(Transcription notes: some speaker labels approximate; minor mis-transcriptions expected: 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'KV cash', 'VPC' sometimes 'V-P-C'.)
